channel.title: Travel AI Monitor
channel.description: Sourced data on how artificial intelligence is reshaping travel and tourism.

item.title: How many travellers use AI to plan trips?
item.description: Between 18% and 79%, depending on what is being asked. The defensible summary: roughly half to two-thirds of travellers have used AI somewhere in a trip, and around one in five uses generative AI specifically to plan one.

item.title: Do travellers trust AI for travel information?
item.description: They use it far more than they trust it. 6% of consumers fully trust AI, 42% always fact-check what it tells them, and 25% have received travel information from it that was outdated or wrong.

item.title: Will travellers let AI book travel for them?
item.description: Mostly not yet. About 12% are comfortable with AI making independent decisions, around 6% would let it handle most of their planning, and a quarter to a third would let it complete a booking they had already specified.

item.title: Is AI replacing search engines for travel research?
item.description: It is displacing channels rather than replacing search outright. AI assistants are now a more trusted planning source (24%) than travel bloggers (19%) or social media influencers (14%), and 69% of Millennials use AI as often as social media for trip planning.

item.title: What do travellers actually use AI for?
item.description: Researching attractions, restaurants and transport (60%), comparing prices (56%), in-trip translation (45%), building itineraries (43%) and destination research (38%). Synthesis tasks dominate; transaction tasks lag.

item.title: How many hotels and tourism businesses use AI?
item.description: Around 70% of tourism businesses use AI, mainly for chatbots, dynamic pricing and demand forecasting. But adoption is strongly size-dependent, and operational AI is not the same as being visible in AI answers.

item.title: Are destinations ready for AI search?
item.description: Not yet. 22% of DMOs offer AI trip planning on their site and 26% have a documented AI strategy, while around 40% of European national tourism organisations have a dedicated AI team or monitor AI use.

item.title: How big is the gap between travellers and the travel industry on AI?
item.description: Roughly two years, by the publisher's own framing. 54% of travellers plan with AI; 22% of destinations offer it. 72% of destination leaders say two more years of inaction risks irrelevance.

item.title: Does AI change where people actually travel?
item.description: Yes. 40% of travellers discovered a destination through AI and 29% changed their plans based on an AI recommendation. And about half of travellers who see an AI answer in a search engine still click through to the source.

item.title: How accurate is AI travel information?
item.description: 25% of travellers report receiving outdated or inaccurate travel information from AI, and that counts only the errors they noticed.

item.title: Which generation uses AI most for travel?
item.description: Millennials, narrowly. 69% use AI as often as social media for trip planning, against 63% of Gen Z.

item.title: How much is AI worth to the travel industry?
item.description: The most-cited figure is Euromonitor's projection of USD 1.4 trillion of travel spending growth over five years attributed to AI-unlocked potential. It is a forecast, not a measurement.

item.title: Are airlines and travel agencies using AI agents?
item.description: Adoption is near-universal and return is not. 80% of travel agencies have already implemented AI and the remaining 20% plan to, and 52% of executives across industries report agents running in production, but only 40% of the AI-adopting agencies report a measurable gain.

item.title: Where in the world is AI travel adoption highest?
item.description: Latin America leads on enthusiasm (98% excited) and Asia Pacific follows (95%). North America and Europe are the most sceptical. Usage intensity measured by telemetry does not follow market size at all.

item.title: How do I get my hotel recommended by ChatGPT?
item.description: Make current, specific, structured facts about the property reachable by machines, keep them fresh, and make sure the third-party sources models already trust describe you accurately.

item.title: Is AI use in travel still growing, or has it plateaued?
item.description: Still growing. Generative AI travel planning grew 64% year on year to 18%, US travellers using AI on at least one trip went 33% to 43% to 56% across three consecutive waves, and intent runs well ahead of behaviour on both US and global measures.

item.title: Does blocking AI crawlers in robots.txt keep my hotel out of ChatGPT?
item.description: It stops the scheduled crawlers. It does not reliably stop a fetch a person triggered, because three of the four major assistant makers publish that robots.txt may not apply to those.

item.title: Do I need an llms.txt file to appear in AI answers?
item.description: Not for Google, which states in writing that no new file, markup or schema is needed. No assistant maker has published that it reads llms.txt.

item.title: Which sources do AI assistants cite when asked about hotels?
item.description: Mostly intermediaries. Online travel agencies took 55.3% of citations in an audit of 1,357 Gemini citations, but the share flips by question type: non-OTA sources take 55.9% of experiential queries.

item.title: Is traffic from AI assistants worth anything yet?
item.description: Small in volume, better in quality. On one destination portal with 1.6 million sessions it converted at 8.26% against 3.88% for organic search.

item.title: How many hotels are invisible in AI search?
item.description: Nobody knows, and the figure everyone quotes does not survive checking. We went looking for the source of the widely cited 94% and could not find one.

item.title: US travellers who have used AI to plan a trip: 54%
item.description: 54% of US travellers had used AI to plan travel as of April 2026, according to Sojern's survey of 1,006 US adults.

item.title: US travellers who intend to use AI for future trips: 75%
item.description: 75% of US travellers say they intend to use AI for future trips, against 54% who have already done so.

item.title: Consumers using AI for trip planning: 51%
item.description: 51% of consumers said they use AI for trip planning in Euromonitor's Voice of the Consumer: Travel Survey, fielded January–February 2025.

item.title: Consumers who have used AI in some travel context: 67%
item.description: 67% of consumers have used AI in some travel context, from a Booking.com survey of 37,325 people across 33 markets.

item.title: Consumers who want to use AI in future travel planning: 89%
item.description: 89% of consumers want to use AI in future travel planning, from the same 33-market Booking.com survey.

item.title: Travellers using generative AI to plan travel: 18%
item.description: 18% of global travellers used generative AI for travel planning in 2025, up from 11% the year before (a 64% increase).

item.title: Travellers who have used AI for trip planning or management: ~79%
item.description: Around 79% of travellers have used AI for trip planning or trip management, per Amadeus research conducted in March 2026.

item.title: Frequent travellers comfortable using AI for trip planning: 80%
item.description: 80% of frequent travellers say they are comfortable using AI for trip planning, per Travelport's State of Modern Retailing.

item.title: US travellers using generative AI for trip planning: ~25%
item.description: Nearly a quarter of US travellers used generative AI tools for trip planning in late 2025, three times the 2022 level, per Deloitte.

item.title: Travellers who find generative AI results helpful: 78%
item.description: 78% of travellers found generative AI results somewhat or very helpful, for planning and in destination alike.

item.title: Millennials using AI as often as social media for trip planning: 69%
item.description: 69% of Millennials and 63% of Gen Z use AI as often as social media when planning a trip.

item.title: Gen Z using AI as often as social media for trip planning: 63%
item.description: 63% of Gen Z travellers use AI as often as social media for trip planning, slightly below Millennials at 69%.

item.title: Consumers who fully trust AI: 6%
item.description: Only 6% of consumers fully trust AI, even though 91% say they are excited about it.

item.title: Consumers comfortable with AI making independent decisions: 12%
item.description: 12% of consumers are comfortable with AI making independent decisions; 25% are unsure and 10% feel very uncomfortable.

item.title: Travellers comfortable letting AI handle most of their planning: ~6%
item.description: Around 6% of travellers are comfortable letting AI handle most of their travel planning, even though about 79% have used AI for travel.

item.title: Travellers ready to let AI handle a booking: 25–33%
item.description: Between a quarter and a third of travellers, depending on the market, are ready to book inside a generative AI platform or let an assistant book for them.

item.title: Consumers who always fact-check AI outputs: 42%
item.description: 42% of consumers always fact-check AI outputs and a further 29% do so sometimes.

item.title: Consumers who trust travel brands to use AI responsibly: 42%
item.description: 42% of consumers trust travel brands to use AI responsibly, placing travel in the top three industries for AI trust.

item.title: Travellers who received outdated or inaccurate AI travel information: 25%
item.description: 25% of travellers report having received outdated or inaccurate travel information from AI.

item.title: Share of consumers classified as AI enthusiasts: 36%
item.description: 36% of consumers are AI Enthusiasts and 25% are Detractors, with Advocates at 13%, Cautious at 13% and Sceptics at 9%.

item.title: North Americans who rarely or never trust AI-generated information: 32%
item.description: 32% in North America and 29% in Europe and the Middle East rarely or never trust AI-generated information, against 15% in Latin America and 16% in Asia Pacific.

item.title: Latin American respondents excited about AI: 98%
item.description: 98% of Latin American respondents are excited about AI, with 89% familiar with it, the highest of any region.

item.title: AI assistants as a trusted travel planning source: 24%
item.description: Yes. AI assistants rank as a trusted travel planning source for 24% of consumers, against 19% for travel bloggers and 14% for social media influencers.

item.title: Travellers who discovered a destination via AI: 40%
item.description: 40% of travellers say they discovered a destination through AI, and 29% changed their plans based on an AI recommendation.

item.title: Travellers who changed plans based on AI recommendations: 29%
item.description: 29% of travellers changed their travel plans based on an AI recommendation.

item.title: Largest travel companies mentioning AI in annual reports: 35%
item.description: 35% of the Skift Travel 200 mentioned AI in their 2024 annual reports, up from about 4% in 2022.

item.title: Share of travel venture funding going to AI-enabled startups: 45%
item.description: 45% of travel venture capital funding went to AI-enabled startups in the first half of 2025, up from about 10% in 2023.

item.title: US travellers who used AI on at least one trip: 56%
item.description: 56% of US travellers used AI for planning, booking or in-destination help on at least one trip in the past twelve months, up from 43% six months earlier and 33% the half-year before that.

item.title: Travellers who still click through after an AI answer: ~50%
item.description: About half of travellers who see an AI answer in a search engine still click through to the source websites.

item.title: DMOs producing AI-formatted content: 64%
item.description: 64% of destination organisations now create AI-formatted content (lists, FAQs and structured answers) to match how AI engines retrieve information.
